newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. to protest to Cyprus over harassment.
newsitem.headline: U.N. to protest to Cyprus over harassment.

text.p: The United Nations Force in Cyprus said on Sunday it would make a formal complaint to the island's government over the harassment of its commander and a group of friends at the hands of Greek Cypriot demonstrators.

United Nations Force in Cyprus (UNICYP) spokesman Waldemar Rokoszewski said protesters tried to stop a group led by Finnish Brigadier-General Ahti Toimi Paavali Vartiainen from crossing into the Turkish-occupied north of the Mediterranean island.
"This is a serious issue. I cannot recall any such incident in the past," he told the semi-official Cyprus News Agency.

Organised groups of Greek Cypriots have recently held demonstrations every weekend at the Ledra Palace Checkpoint, the only crossing into northern Cyprus, to protest against the Turkish occupation of this part of the island.

Last month police used tear gas to disperse about 50 protesters who had tried to stop British and U.S. diplomats from crossing to the Turkish zone. Five people were admitted to hospital with breathing problems.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded the northern third of the island in 1974 in the wake of a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling Greece at the time.
U.N. troops patrol the zone dividing the island.
